expected_points: Be clear about which customers have the problem your product solves and why.

answer.summary: Pete recommends defining the ICP precisely—who has the problem and why—so founders spend less time on poor-fit prospects and more sales conversations with strong-fit customers. Distinguish the target company from the people involved in its buying process.

sections.heading: Define fit clearly, then focus sales effort
sections.content: Be “very crisp” about which customers have the problem and why. Use that definition to judge whether an organization is a strong opportunity or one to pass on, avoiding wasted time and doing more sales loops with prospects at the “white-hot center” of fit.

sections.heading: Separate company fit from buyer personas
sections.content: For B2B sales, define both the account’s characteristics and the humans involved. Pete’s Amplitude example: a fitting organization makes software products and likely has at least a couple of product managers. The product managers may use the product, engineering may assess technical integration, and the budget owner may be the VP of Product, VP of Engineering, or CTO. Knowing those roles helps founders target the right organization and navigate its buying process.
